core_obligations: Exploit the normalization (proof lines 10227-10236): the normalization nu : X^nu -> X is a universal homeomorphism, so it induces an isomorphism on etale fundamental groups and an equivalence between finite type locally constant Lambda-modules on X_etale and on X^nu_etale; this reduces the lemma to the case where X is integral and normal.

Sheaf to representation (proof lines 10239-10263): for an integral normal X with generic point eta, a finite type locally constant Lambda-module on X_etale has finitely many sections over the generic point, and the action of pi_1(X, etabar) on that finite module is continuous, which produces the functor to representations.

Representation to sheaf (proof lines 10266-10291): conversely, from a finite Lambda-module M with a continuous action of pi_1(X, etabar) the author constructs a finite type locally constant sheaf on X_etale whose generic fibre is M, using the description of such sheaves as those trivialised by a finite Galois covering, and checks that the two constructions are inverse.
proof_roadmap: Replace X by its normalization, a universal homeomorphism, so the etale site and the fundamental group do not change.
In the integral normal case, send a finite type locally constant sheaf to its finite module of generic sections with its continuous fundamental group action.
Conversely, build a finite type locally constant sheaf from a finite module with continuous action by trivialising along finite Galois coverings.
Check that the two constructions are mutually inverse.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the standard classification of locally constant sheaves to irreducible geometrically unibranch schemes, and the point of the extension is that a finite Lambda-module need not have a finite underlying set, so the proof of the companion lemma does not apply as written (statement lines 10199-10219, with the author's remark at proof lines 10221-10224 recording exactly that failure). The proof has three steps: the reduction to the normal case through the normalization morphism and the invariance of the etale site under universal homeomorphisms (proof lines 10227-10236); the construction of the functor from finite type locally constant sheaves to finite modules with continuous fundamental group action in the integral normal case (proof lines 10239-10263); and the converse construction together with the verification that the two are inverse (proof lines 10266-10291). The non-formal content is the finiteness discussion that the companion proof lacks. The claim is H2: a proof that adapts a known result, with the adaptation itself written out.
